question: Do Transformer MLP neurons form separable, spatially local modules specialized for image classes or text domains, and do activation-selected neurons align with weight-based MoEfication clusters?

key_findings.claim: Selective neuron ablation produces intuitive cross-category damage patterns in one fine-tuned ViT and one Mistral-7B model.
key_findings.evidence: For CIFAR-20 superclasses, pruning neurons selected for insects also harms non-insect invertebrates, while aquatic categories covary. For Mistral, selections associated with PubMed or arXiv reduce several related MMLU subjects. The evidence is presented as heatmaps after tuning each selection size to a target 50/80% ViT or 20% Mistral drop, without numerical tables, repetitions, or inferential statistics.

key_findings.claim: The written neuron score is directionally inconsistent with the stated selection rule.
key_findings.evidence: Equation 1 divides mean absolute activation on the reference dataset by activation on the target/unlearned dataset, yet the paper selects the highest-scoring neurons as relevant to the target and prunes them. A high ratio instead identifies neurons more active on reference than target. Unless the equation, dataset names, or ranking direction is reversed in code, the core localization method cannot have the claimed interpretation.

key_findings.claim: Performance-targeted pruning makes neuron-set sizes vary substantially and confounds task overlap with selection cardinality.
key_findings.evidence: Each task's percentage is chosen after observing how many removals reach an arbitrary damage target; selected sets average 12.5 plus/minus 6.0% in ViT and 3.4 plus/minus 2.6% in Mistral. The overlap |Ni intersect Nj|/|Ni| is asymmetric and rises mechanically with |Nj|, yet no size-matched hypergeometric/Jaccard null or uncertainty is reported.

key_findings.claim: The random-model comparison does not provide evidence for the lottery-ticket hypothesis.
key_findings.evidence: The analysis compares correlations between task-pair overlap matrices computed separately inside a trained model and a single random model. It never tracks the same initialized neurons through training, tests whether a random subnetwork can train to full accuracy, or demonstrates a winning ticket. Similarity can arise solely from shared input/token statistics and the selection procedure.

key_findings.claim: The random ViT and Mistral controls are not performance-matched and may not support the same ablation target.
key_findings.evidence: Only one random seed is used. A randomly initialized classifier/language model has near-chance predictions, so a relative 50-80% class accuracy or 20% next-token drop is unstable and semantically unlike damage to a trained model. The paper does not report random baselines, exact selected percentages, or whether performance targeting was even applied identically.

key_findings.claim: Weight clustering aligns more with selected neurons in trained early/late layers, but the concentration statistic lacks the correct sorted-random baseline.
key_findings.evidence: Balanced k-means partitions input-weight vectors into 96 ViT or 128 Mistral groups. The study sorts cluster counts and reports normalized Lorenz-curve area, where 0.5 is called uniform. With finite randomly assigned selected neurons, sorting alone makes expected area exceed 0.5; the expected value also depends on set size, so trained/random curves cannot be interpreted without permutation intervals.

key_findings.claim: The analysis equates activation magnitude and ablation damage with semantic specialization despite acknowledged polysemanticity and causal interactions.
key_findings.evidence: Selection uses only marginal mean absolute activation ratios, then removes many neurons simultaneously. High activation can be inhibitory, redundant, input-frequency-driven, or compensated by attention/other MLPs; nonlinear group ablation does not assign individual causal function. The paper cites prior evidence that activation magnitude, selectivity, and individual damage are insufficient but does not add interaction-aware controls.

key_findings.claim: Several reported implementation quantities are internally inconsistent or underspecified.
key_findings.evidence: Figure 4 labels the Mistral sets as top 1% while the text and Figure 6 use 3.4 plus/minus 2.6%; the ViT description does not identify the fine-tuning procedure/checkpoint; sample counts, sequence lengths, prompts, activation aggregation over tokens, accuracy denominators, error bars, and seeds are omitted. Figure-only heatmaps prevent reconstruction of the claims.

key_findings.claim: The study demonstrates exploratory task-dependent sensitivity, not modularity as it defines it.
key_findings.evidence: The introduction requires both separability and positional locality. Results show overlapping selected sets and within-layer cluster concentration, but do not locate stable modules in contiguous network positions, test modular recombination, or compare within-module to between-module causal connectivity. Collateral damage is frequently large and asymmetric, which can equally indicate distributed shared representations.

method.core_idea: Rank MLP neurons by relative activation on a broad reference versus a target subset, prune a target-dependent fraction until performance drops, compare selected-set overlap across tasks, and test whether selected neurons concentrate in balanced weight-space clusters.
method.mechanism: Post-activation MLP units are scored from dataset means. Separate selections are made for CIFAR-20 superclasses and text/MMLU domains in trained and random ViT/Mistral models. Balanced k-means on MLP input weights creates pseudo-experts, and a sorted cumulative cluster-count area measures concentration by layer.
assumptions: The score direction in Equation 1 correctly ranks target-relevant neurons.
Mean absolute activation is a useful proxy for causal task importance.
Performance-targeted selections of different sizes can be compared through raw asymmetric overlap.
Random and trained models with radically different performance provide a meaningful structural control.
Euclidean input-weight clusters approximate co-activated functional experts.
Above-uniform sorted cluster concentration indicates semantic locality rather than finite-sample sorting bias.

techniques.role: Ranks post-activation MLP neurons for a data subset.
Chooses enough ranked neurons to induce a preset task-performance decline.
Compares putative task modules across classes and domains.
Partitions each MLP into equal-size pseudo-expert neuron clusters.
Measures whether selected neurons fall into relatively few pseudo-experts.

evaluations.setting: ViT-Base-224 fine-tuned for CIFAR-100 with CIFAR-20 forget classes
evaluations.metric: Relative top-1 accuracy matrix after 50% or 80% target-class damage
evaluations.result: Qualitative heatmaps show collateral damage among intuitively related visual superclasses and reduced selectivity at the stronger target.
evaluations.baseline: Other CIFAR-20 classes and a single randomly initialized ViT.

evaluations.setting: Mistral-7B-Instruct v0.2 across Pile/science/code subsets and zero-shot MMLU subjects
evaluations.metric: Top-1 next-token and MMLU accuracy after a targeted 20% subset drop
evaluations.result: Some related domains co-degrade, but substantial failures and accuracy increases also occur; no numerical or uncertainty table is supplied.
evaluations.baseline: Cross-domain damage matrix and a single random Mistral initialization.

evaluations.setting: Selected neuron sets in trained and random models
evaluations.result: Task-pair overlap patterns are qualitatively correlated across initialization and training, with trained sets often less extremely overlapping.
evaluations.baseline: Randomly initialized model rather than a cardinality-matched random-set null.

evaluations.setting: Layerwise selected sets versus balanced MoEfication clusters
evaluations.metric: Normalized area under sorted cumulative cluster counts
evaluations.result: Trained-model concentration exceeds random-model concentration, strongest in early ViT and early/late Mistral layers.
evaluations.baseline: One random model; no within-model label/cluster permutation interval.

limitations: The central score formula and stated selection direction conflict.
Only two models and one random seed per architecture are studied.
Dataset sizes, prompts, token aggregation, fine-tuning details, exact masks, and most numerical results are missing.
Selected-set size varies by task and raw asymmetric overlap is not corrected for cardinality.
The sorted concentration statistic lacks a finite-sample permutation null.
Random models are not accuracy- or activation-distribution-matched controls.
Marginal activation and group pruning cannot isolate individual neuron function or interactions.
Attention modules are ignored despite carrying task-relevant computation.
The evidence does not satisfy the paper's own positional-locality definition of modularity.
failure_modes: Reversing numerator and denominator selects reference-general rather than target-specific neurons.
Large or high-variance task sets exhibit greater overlap purely from cardinality.
Pruning many correlated neurons triggers nonlinear compensation or global distribution shift.
Domain-specific token frequency and sequence length masquerade as knowledge specialization.
Random-model overlap reflects shared embeddings/input statistics rather than innate functional modules.
Balanced k-means groups nearby weights that never coactivate or serve the same causal role.
Polysemantic neurons make a module appear selective on the measured tasks but fail on unseen functions.
Arbitrary target-damage thresholds change both masks and apparent cross-task relationships.
reusable_insights: Pair task-specific ablation matrices with cardinality-matched random masks and symmetric normalized overlaps.
Treat activation selectivity, causal necessity, sufficiency, and functional modularity as distinct properties.
Track identical neuron identities from initialization through checkpoints before making lottery-ticket claims.
Use layerwise permutations to calibrate any sorted cluster-concentration statistic.
Report complete numerical damage matrices and uncertainty rather than relying on intuitive heatmap reading.
Test whether discovered modules recombine, transfer, and preserve unrelated behaviors on held-out domains.
Include attention and cross-component interactions when claiming Transformer-wide modularity.
open_questions: Is Equation 1 or the highest-score selection rule reversed in the actual implementation?
Do task modules persist under multiple seeds, model families, prompts, and matched dataset statistics?
How much overlap remains after correcting exactly for mask size, layer, activation frequency, and neuron norm?
Can causal-gradient or cooperative-game attribution recover more stable task-specific sets than magnitude ratios?
Do selected neurons retain their function under paraphrase, domain shift, multilingual inputs, and adversarial examples?
Can weight clusters predict activation co-occurrence and causal interaction out of sample?
Does checkpoint tracking show specialization emerging from particular initial subnetworks?
Can modules be swapped or recombined to transfer a capability without broad collateral effects?

competitive_landscape.title: Finding Skill Neurons in Pre-trained Transformer-based Language Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Direct prior localization of task-related Transformer neurons with pruning applications.
competitive_landscape.difference: Wang et al. identify neurons whose activations predict task labels after prompt tuning and validate their relevance across alternative tuning methods. The reviewed paper broadens to vision, domains, random weights, and cluster overlap, but uses a simpler and apparently direction-inconsistent activation ratio.

competitive_landscape.title: Task-specific Compression for Multi-task Language Models using Attribution-based Pruning
competitive_landscape.relationship: Prior task-specific neuron attribution and pruning method with quantitative compression evaluation.
competitive_landscape.difference: Yang et al. use attribution to preserve task-important neurons, benchmark six datasets, and test unseen domains. The reviewed paper focuses instead on cross-task overlap and clustering, but supplies much weaker controls and no compression result.

competitive_landscape.title: Does Large Language Model Contain Task-Specific Neurons?
competitive_landscape.relationship: Near-concurrent direct competitor for task-specific neuron localization.
competitive_landscape.difference: Song et al. use causal gradient variation around task-relevant tokens and validate localization through both inhibition and amplification over eight public tasks. That raises the causal bar beyond the reviewed paper's mean-activation ranking and bulk ablations.

competitive_landscape.title: Neuron Specialization: Leveraging Intrinsic Task Modularity for Multilingual Machine Translation
competitive_landscape.relationship: Concurrent application of neuron overlap as functional task modularity.
competitive_landscape.difference: Tan et al. trace language-specific-to-shared specialization across layers and turn it into sparse multilingual training with performance gains. The reviewed paper spans more heterogeneous domains but stops at qualitative maps and does not demonstrate a modular training or inference benefit.

competitive_landscape.title: Towards Understanding Multi-Task Learning Generalization of LLMs via Detecting and Exploring Task-Specific Neurons
competitive_landscape.relationship: Later direct study linking task-neuron overlap to transfer and forgetting.
competitive_landscape.difference: Leng and Xiong use gradient attribution, extensive deactivation/fine-tuning, and continuous-learning experiments to connect overlap with generalization and catastrophic forgetting. It operationalizes several interpretations that remain qualitative in the reviewed paper.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims evidence that Transformer MLP neurons form task-specific modules, that related tasks share them, that partial structure exists at random initialization, and that trained selected neurons align with MoEfication clusters especially in boundary layers.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Task/skill-neuron localization, attribution pruning, MoEfication, clusterability, and emergent modularity all predate the paper. Its distinctive contribution is combining performance-targeted selection, trained/random task-overlap matrices, and pseudo-expert concentration across one vision and one language model.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The combination is exploratory rather than a strong modularity result. A likely score-direction error, size-confounded overlap, uncalibrated concentration, and an invalid lottery-ticket inference undermine the central conclusions. Later concurrent work provides more causal localization and functional use. Novelty is modest and evidential confidence in specialization is low until the implementation and null models are repaired.

reviewer_notes: Read all 11 extracted pages, including equations, every heatmap caption, clustering statistic, related work, and limitations. The audit checked score direction, overlap cardinality, random-model comparability, lottery-ticket logic, and sorted-area calibration. Competing papers were checked through primary ACL, arXiv, OpenReview, and PMLR records current through 2026-08-23. No code execution or replication was performed.
